findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric service routing to four transformer pads and buildings. However, no documentation is provided confirming whether the site is within the Downtown Network Area boundaries per UCM § 1.11.5 Network Area Map. The grouping explicitly states 'Network Area determination requires cross-referencing the project address against the official Network Area Map... as this cannot be determined from site plans alone.' No duct bank design for a Network distribution system loop is visible on any sheets. The Master Comment Report references a Bluebeam review from Austin Energy but those comments are not provided in the submitted documentation.
findings.reasoning: Applicability of EL-19.1 depends entirely on confirming that the site is within Network Area boundaries AND will tie into Network distribution system. The project address (3759 Valley View Road, Austin TX 78704, South Lamar area) location relative to the downtown Network Area cannot be verified from the site plan documents alone. No Network Area determination letter or ESPA documentation is provided. Without this external verification, the applicability cannot be confirmed, and therefore the deficiency cannot be definitively assessed.
findings.comment: Network Area status must be verified by cross-reference to the official Network Area Map per UCM § 1.11.5. If site is within Network Area, duct bank design coordination with Austin Energy Network Design (512-505-7682) must be documented on the electrical sheets.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed underground electric lines with routing from transformers to pull boxes and building meters. However, no loop system design is depicted, labeled, or referenced on this or any other sheet. The grouping states applicability is 'Only when loop system is required for the site per Austin Energy service requirements.' No Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) approval letter or Austin Energy correspondence confirming loop system requirement is present in the submitted documentation. The Master Comment Report's Electric Review section references Bluebeam comments (not provided) which may contain details about loop system requirements.
findings.reasoning: Loop system is a specialized service configuration required only in certain Austin Energy network conditions. The preliminary site plan documents do not include ESPA approval documentation that would clarify whether a loop system is required for this project. Without the ESPA determination, the applicability cannot be confirmed. The grouping explicitly requires 'Austin Energy ESPA approval letters and correspondence confirming loop system requirement' to establish applicability.
findings.comment: Obtain Austin Energy ESPA approval documentation to determine if loop system is required for this site. If required, show loop system design on all applicable plan sheets per UCM § 1.10.4.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows what appears to be a single electrical service configuration with four transformer pads serving the 39 townhome units. No dual feed electrical service is mentioned in the electrical design, electrical load calculations, or on any plan sheets. No Austin Energy approval letter specifically addressing dual feed is present in the submitted documentation. The grouping states applicability is 'Only when dual feed service is requested,' which appears not to be the case based on the preliminary design shown.
findings.reasoning: Dual feed service is a specialized configuration where a site receives power from two separate Austin Energy service points. This is typically requested for large commercial or critical facilities requiring redundancy. The preliminary electrical design shown on Sheet 21 does not indicate a dual feed configuration. Without evidence of a dual feed request, this item appears not applicable. However, the final determination cannot be confirmed without Austin Energy ESPA documentation.
findings.comment: If dual feed electricity service is being requested, provide electrical load calculations, service configuration details on the electrical site plan, and Austin Energy approval letter specifically addressing dual feed service per UCM § 1.5.2.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed transformer pads and underground service routing to the buildings. No plan notes reference line extension, Contributions in Aid of Construction (CIAC), line extension fees, or any line extension requirements. The grouping states that line extension determination 'cannot be determined from site plans alone' and 'is made exclusively by Austin Energy during the Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) review process.' No ESPA approval documentation is provided in the submitted plans or supplementary documents. The Master Comment Report confirms 'AE completeness check complete' but the actual ESPA letter with line extension determination is not provided.
findings.reasoning: Whether a line extension is required to serve the site is a technical determination made exclusively by Austin Energy during ESPA review based on existing infrastructure capacity and location. This determination is not visible in the site plan documents. Without the ESPA documentation that contains Austin Energy's line extension determination, the applicability cannot be confirmed. The preliminary electrical design assumes service is available, but whether extension of existing infrastructure is required remains undetermined.
findings.comment: Obtain and provide Austin Energy's Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) approval letter which contains the determination of whether line extension is required to serve the site, and if required, documentation of Contributions in Aid of Construction (CIAC) or line extension fees per UCM § 1.3.12.

findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) includes Site Plan Release Note item (e) stating 'Water and wastewater service will be provided by the City of Austin (or identify the service provider if other than the City of Austin).' This phrasing indicates the service provider for water/wastewater may not be confirmed as City of Austin. However, the equivalent note for electrical service is not explicit on the plans. The site location is in Austin city limits (jurisdiction confirmed as 'City of Austin — Full Purpose'), but specific verification that the site is within Austin Energy's electrical service territory is not documented on the plans or in supplementary documents. Without explicit confirmation of Austin Energy service territory inclusion, compliance with Code of Ordinances § 15-9-1 cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: Code of Ordinances § 15-9-1 establishes service territory boundaries. Sites outside Austin Energy's service territory must have all Austin Energy references and notes removed from plans. Conversely, sites within the territory must maintain appropriate Austin Energy references. The grouping requires 'site location relative to Austin Energy service boundaries' and states 'if outside AE territory, plans should not reference AE standards.' The submission contains multiple Austin Energy design criteria references (Sheet 3 transmission clearances, Master Comment Report electric review), which implies territory inclusion, but explicit confirmation is not provided.
findings.comment: Confirm in writing that the site at 3759 Valley View Road is within Austin Energy's service territory. If confirmed, ensure all Austin Energy standards and references remain on plans. If outside service territory, remove all Austin Energy references and notes from plans.

codeCitations: Texas Public Utility Regulatory Act (state law)
applicableAreas: Service provider selection in dual territory areas
findings.observation: No documentation is provided indicating whether the site is located in a dual service area where both Austin Energy and another utility provider operate. No Public Utility Commission Service Area Exception Application or service provider selection documentation is present in the submitted materials. The grouping states applicability is 'Only when development is in dual service area between Austin Energy and another provider AND requests service from non-territorial provider.' No evidence of this scenario is apparent from the site plan documents or supplementary files.
findings.reasoning: PUC Service Area Exception Applications are required only when a customer in a dual service area (where both Austin Energy and another provider operate) requests service from the non-territorial provider. This is a state-level regulatory requirement under the Texas Public Utility Regulatory Act. The site location relative to dual service areas cannot be determined from site plan documents alone, and no service provider selection documentation is provided that would indicate this is applicable. The grouping explicitly requires 'Service territory maps, provider selection documentation, PUC application submittal' to assess this item.
findings.comment: Determine whether the site is in a dual service area between Austin Energy and another utility provider. If so, and if non-territorial service is requested, complete and submit the Public Utility Commission Service Area Exception Application per Texas Public Utility Regulatory Act.

findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) exists and shows proposed landscape planting and site features. An irrigation system appears to be proposed as part of the landscape design, as indicated by the landscape plan content. However, no irrigation plan submission to Austin Energy is documented in the supplementary documents. The grouping states applicability is 'Only when irrigation system is proposed and Austin Energy coordination is required per ESPA process.' The Master Comment Report does not list irrigation review as a requirement, and no ESPA documentation is provided that would clarify whether Austin Energy irrigation review is required during site plan vs. building plan stage.
findings.reasoning: Irrigation system coordination with Austin Energy is required under specific ESPA conditions related to distribution capacity and coordination with underground electric infrastructure. The grouping requires 'Landscape plans, irrigation design, Austin Energy correspondence indicating irrigation review requirement' to establish applicability. While a landscape plan exists, the specific determination that Austin Energy irrigation review is required at the site plan stage is not documented. Irrigation plan review may be deferred to building permit stage. Without the ESPA documentation or explicit Austin Energy requirement, applicability cannot be confirmed.
findings.comment: If Austin Energy irrigation review is required per ESPA process, submit an irrigation plan to Austin Energy showing proposed irrigation routing, line locations, and coordination with underground electric infrastructure per UCM Section 1.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts proposed electric service routing including four transformer pad locations, underground electric lines connecting to buildings, pull boxes, and electrical meters. However, the electrical design plan contains zero references to the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM), no compliance statements with specific UCM sections (such as § 1.3.12, 1.9.3, 1.10.3, 1.10.4), and no notation of design standard compliance. The Master Comment Report lists required Austin Energy Design Criteria sections (UCM § 1.3.8, 1.3.12, 1.3.16, 1.9.3, 1.10.3, 1.10.4, 1.10.10.3 & 4) but these standards are not referenced on the electrical sheets themselves. The grouping states this requirement applies to 'All sites' requiring connection to Austin Energy system.
findings.reasoning: The checklist deficiency states 'Proposed electric service routing not shown in accordance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual.' The site plan documents show routing (transformer locations, line paths, connections), but this routing is not explicitly documented as compliant with or designed according to UCM standards. The absence of any UCM section references on the electrical sheet means the design cannot be demonstrated to meet the required standards. Professional practice requires that electrical service design reference and comply with the applicable design manual. The grouping specifies this is required for 'All sites requiring connection to Austin Energy system,' which applies here.
findings.comment: Add notes to the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan referencing compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1) and specifically identify which UCM sections govern the proposed service routing (e.g., UCM § 1.3.12 Line Extension Policy, UCM § 1.9.3 Metering Equipment, UCM § 1.10.3 Overhead Line Clearances, UCM § 1.10.4 Padmount Equipment Clearances). Demonstrate that proposed service routing is designed in accordance with these standards.

applicableAreas: Existing overhead electric lines and proposed building locations
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows dashed lines labeled 'OHE' (Overhead Electric) running along the southern and western property boundaries/Right-of-Way. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts all eight buildings positioned within the site interior. The proximity of proposed buildings to existing overhead electric conductors is evident from the plan layout. However, no clearance dimension analysis, conflict assessment, or documentation of Austin Energy clearance discussion is visible on either sheet or in the supplementary documents. Sheet 3 contains a note about 'Electric Transmission Clearances' but this is a general note, not a site-specific conflict analysis. No Austin Energy coordination documentation or clearance letter addressing specific conflicts is provided.
findings.reasoning: The checklist deficiency states 'Clearance conflict between existing electric conductors and proposed buildings not discussed with and resolved by Austin Energy Design.' The site plan clearly shows existing overhead electric infrastructure (OHE lines on the perimeter) and proposes buildings in proximity to these lines. The code requires that clearance issues be 'discussed with and resolved by Austin Energy Design.' The absence of any clearance analysis, conflict resolution documentation, or Austin Energy coordination letter indicates this requirement has not been met. While buildings may not physically encroach the conductors, the site plan does not demonstrate that clearance conflicts (if any exist) have been addressed through proper Austin Energy engineering evaluation.
findings.comment: Coordinate with Austin Energy regarding clearance between existing overhead electric conductors (OHE lines shown on property perimeter) and proposed buildings. Obtain Austin Energy clearance determination addressing any potential conflicts and document resolution on the electrical site plan per UCM § 1.10.4.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 is labeled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' (emphasis on preliminary). The Master Comment Report confirms 'AE completeness check complete' from Victor Givens (Austin Energy), indicating completeness review has occurred. However, no stamped Austin Energy approval letter is provided in the submitted documentation. The Master Comment Report's Electric Review section references a Bluebeam link for Austin Energy comments (https://studio.bluebeam.com/share/epcafnizivuefw), but the actual Austin Energy approval letter and stamped electrical site plan required by LDC § 25-4-200 are not included in the submitted supplementary documents. The grouping specifically requires 'Austin Energy approval letter, stamped electrical site plan, ESPA approval documentation' to establish compliance.
findings.reasoning: LDC § 25-4-200 requires that 'all electric system plans for subdivisions and sites requiring connection to Austin Energy's system must obtain approval from Austin Energy.' The statute mandates approval, not merely preliminary review. The submission of a 'Preliminary' electrical design plan without an accompanying Austin Energy approval letter does not satisfy this requirement. The completeness check confirmation indicates that Austin Energy has reviewed the plans for completeness (procedural conformance), but approval (substantive compliance with design standards) is a separate and more rigorous determination. Without the formal approval letter and stamped site plan, this requirement is not satisfied.
findings.comment: Obtain and submit a stamped Austin Energy approval letter for the electrical site plan and the Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) approval per LDC § 25-4-200. The approval must address the proposed electric system design and confirm compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1).

applicableAreas: Electrical service design and equipment placement
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts transformer pad locations, underground electric service routing, pull boxes, and electrical meters. However, the sheet contains no notes, callouts, or references demonstrating compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM). No clearances are dimensioned according to UCM § 1.10.4 tables. No equipment placement notes reference specific UCM standards. The transformer pads are shown as generic rectangular symbols with no detail references or specification callouts. The grouping requires 'Electrical site plan includes UCM compliance notes, clearances dimensioned per UCM § 1.10.4, equipment placement meets UCM standards, transformer locations comply with Table 1.10.4 requirements.' None of these compliance demonstrations are visible on the electrical sheets.
findings.reasoning: The deficiency states 'Compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual not demonstrated.' The electrical design plan shows the proposed infrastructure layout but provides no evidence that this design was created with reference to UCM standards or that it meets those standards. Professional engineering practice and the code requirement for LDC § 25-4-200 compliance mandate that the design be explicitly documented as meeting the applicable design manual. Specificity is required: the sheet must show which UCM sections apply (e.g., § 1.10.4 for transformer clearances), what the requirements are (e.g., minimum 10-foot clearance from hot-stick use area), and how the proposed design meets them (dimensioned clearances and compliance notes). The absence of all this documentation is the deficiency.
findings.comment: Revise the electrical site plan to include compliance notes referencing specific UCM sections. Dimension clearances around transformer pads per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4, specifying: (1) hot-stick use area (pad-locked sides) = 10 feet minimum clearance, (2) facing confined space (niche/vault) = 15 feet, (3) oil-filled equipment to fire escape/stairs = 20 feet, (4) adjacent brick/masonry building = 5 feet minimum, (5) adjacent non-brick/masonry building = 12 feet from oil-filled equipment. Add notes confirming equipment pad placement within 6 feet of parking/traffic areas for truck access and specifying bollard requirements if within 4 feet. Transformer pads must be 2 feet from back of sidewalks.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) at the site plan stage shows only a high-level service routing diagram with transformer locations, underground line routing, pull boxes, and meters. The distinction between Austin Energy-owned infrastructure (up to meter) and customer-owned infrastructure (from meter/load side) is not explicitly shown or labeled on the site plan. The specific identification of customer-owned conduit and cable on the load side of the meter typically requires building electrical plans with detailed electrical room design and service panel locations. The grouping states applicability is 'Only when customer-owned conduit and cable on load side of meter is proposed' and requires 'Electrical service design, meter location, ownership boundaries; customer-owned facilities beyond meter point are under City Electrical Inspector jurisdiction, not Austin Energy.'
findings.reasoning: This deficiency addresses a jurisdictional issue: customer-owned facilities beyond the meter point fall under City of Austin Building/Electrical Inspector jurisdiction, not Austin Energy jurisdiction. The site plan documents do not show the interior building electrical design or meter room configuration that would clarify where the meter is located and what facilities are customer-owned. This determination requires building electrical plans rather than site plan review. However, to avoid future confusion, the site plan should either clarify this boundary or the building plans must show the proper jurisdictional delineation.
findings.comment: Building electrical plans must clearly show the meter location and electrical service configuration, with explicit labeling of the boundary between Austin Energy-owned facilities (up to and including meter) and customer-owned facilities (load side of meter). Customer-owned conduit and cable are under City Electrical Inspector jurisdiction and should not be submitted for Austin Energy approval. This determination cannot be made from site plan review alone; verification is required during building plan stage.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows four 'Electrical Transformer Pad' locations depicted as rectangular symbols. These appear to be pad-mounted transformers (clear-to-sky installation), not subsurface vaults or enclosed transformer rooms. The grouping states 'Only when vaults or subsurface/enclosed transformer rooms are proposed' and requires applicability assessment. UCM § 1.5.2.6 states 'Transformer Installation Requirements (vaults restricted to Network Area).' Pad-mounted transformers are permissible outside the Network Area. However, the Network Area status of the site at 3759 Valley View Road, Austin TX 78704 has not been verified from site plans or in the documentation. Without Network Area determination, and given that the transformers shown are pad-mounted (not vaults), this item appears to have limited applicability. However, if a vault installation were proposed, Network Area confirmation would be critical.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.5.2.6 restricts transformer vaults exclusively to the Network Area. Outside the Network Area, only pad-mounted (clear-to-sky) transformers or specialized niches meeting specific requirements (35-foot vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls, accessible from outside, proper ventilation, truck accessibility per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3) are permitted. The site plan shows pad-mounted transformers, which are compliant outside the Network Area. The Network Area determination cannot be verified from site plans. If the site is actually within the Network Area and the transformers should be vaults instead, or if specialized niches are being proposed, this would need verification. Without the Network Area map cross-reference, definitive assessment is unclear.
findings.comment: Verify the site location relative to the Austin Energy Network Area Map (UCM § 1.11.5) at https://mcclibrary.blob.core.usgovcloudapi.com/codecontent/15312/483105/1-11-5.png. If the site is within the Network Area, confirm transformer installation is vault-type per UCM § 1.5.2.6. If outside the Network Area, confirm transformers are pad-mounted (as shown) or, if enclosed, demonstrate they meet specialized niche requirements: 35-foot vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls/ceilings, accessible from outside the building, proper ventilation, and truck accessibility per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3.

findings.observation: The Site Plan (Sheet 9) provides overall site layout and building footprints for eight multi-unit townhome buildings. Visual analysis of the site plan found 'no rooms within the building footprints labeled as electrical rooms' and 'no doors explicitly labeled or marked as electrical room doors on any of the buildings.' The interior building electrical room design and door configuration are architectural/building plan elements not typically depicted on site plans. The grouping states applicability is 'Only when electrical room is provided in building' and requires 'Building plans, electrical room design, exterior access per Austin Energy requirements.' These details are documented on building electrical plans, not site plans.
findings.reasoning: Electrical room exterior door requirements are specified in Austin Energy design standards (UCM Section 1) to ensure that Austin Energy service personnel can access metering and service equipment without entering tenant-occupied spaces. This is a building-level design requirement verified during building plan review, not a site plan-level requirement. The site plan review stage does not typically include verification of interior building room configurations or door placements. This deficiency should be assessed during building electrical plan review with the City Electrical Inspector and Austin Energy reviewers.
findings.comment: Electrical room design and exterior door access requirements will be verified during building plan review per Austin Energy requirements under UCM Section 1. Building electrical plans must show each electrical room with an exterior-accessible door for Austin Energy service access, proper clearances, ventilation, and fire-rated walls as required.

findings.observation: No construction phase site plan or construction management plan is included in the submitted site plan documents. Safety signage for existing Austin Energy facilities during construction is typically detailed on construction management plans, erosion control plans with safety details, or a dedicated safety/construction phasing plan. These documents are not among the submitted site plan sheets (Sheets 1-39). The grouping states applicability is 'Only when existing Austin Energy facilities (transformers, vaults, conductors, equipment) are present on construction site' and requires 'Existing utility locations, construction staging plans, protective signage details.'
findings.reasoning: While existing Austin Energy facilities (overhead electric lines shown on the property perimeter, eventual transformer pad installations) will be present during construction, the specific safety signage requirements are a construction management detail typically addressed in construction phase documents rather than site plan phase documents. The site plan stage is preliminary design; construction management and safety signage are detailed during the construction document phase. This item would be more appropriately assessed during permitting for grading, erosion control, and building permits when construction sequencing and safety plans are finalized.
findings.comment: During construction permitting and plan approval, provide a Construction Management Plan detailing existing Austin Energy facility locations and required protective signage per UCM § 1.10.1. Signage must warn contractors of all existing Austin Energy facilities (overhead lines, future transformer pads) and specify clearance requirements. Coordinate with Austin Energy regarding protective barriers and safety measures.

findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) contains a section titled 'Electric Transmission Notes' referencing transmission clearances and UCM transmission requirements. Sheet 21 shows dashed lines labeled 'OHE' (Overhead Electric) running along the property perimeter. However, the voltage class of these overhead electric lines is not specified on either sheet. The grouping defines 'Transmission vs. Distribution Facilities' as transmission being ≥60kV phase-to-phase (Austin Energy operates at 69kV, 138kV, or 345kV) and distribution being <60kV (typically 12.5kV). The sheet notes and visual depiction do not identify whether the existing OHE lines are transmission-class (69kV+) or distribution-class (12.5kV), making it impossible to determine if the transmission safety meeting requirement applies.
findings.reasoning: The tailgate safety meeting requirement per UCM § 1.14.0 applies only when site work is 'adjacent to or affects transmission facilities' defined as ≥60kV. Distribution facilities (12.5kV) have different, less stringent requirements. The site plan documents show existing overhead electric lines but do not specify their voltage class. Transmission structures are 'substantially larger—taller poles, wider spacing, conductors spread further apart' than distribution, but without explicit voltage information or structural descriptions confirming transmission-class infrastructure, the voltage level cannot be determined from the plans alone. This determination would require coordination with Austin Energy to identify the existing line voltage.
findings.comment: Coordinate with Austin Energy to determine the voltage class of existing overhead electric (OHE) lines shown on the property perimeter. If lines are transmission-class (69kV or higher), implement the tailgate safety meeting requirement with Austin Energy Transmission C&M per UCM § 1.14.0 and add the requirement to construction documents. If distribution-class (<60kV), standard distribution clearance and safety requirements apply.

findings.observation: No construction methodology plan, equipment plan, or crane use documentation is included in the submitted site plan documents. The grouping states applicability is 'Only when cranes will be used during construction near Austin Energy facilities.' The site plan depicts eight multi-story townhome buildings (up to 6-plex units) on a 2.16-acre site in a residential area. Construction of these buildings will likely require crane use for heavy material handling and roof assembly, and the site is adjacent to existing overhead electric lines. However, specific crane operation plans and proximity analysis are construction document-level details, not site plan-level details.
findings.reasoning: Crane safety requirements per UCM § 1.14.3.2 address operational safety during construction when cranes are in proximity to electric facilities. Detailed crane operating plans, equipment specifications, and crew safety briefing requirements are documented during the construction document and permitting phases, not the site plan phase. While the site plan provides sufficient information to infer that cranes may be needed and electric facilities exist, the specific crane safety documentation cannot be assessed at the site plan review stage. This should be addressed during building permit and construction document review.
findings.comment: If cranes or other mechanical equipment will be used during construction near existing Austin Energy facilities (existing OHE lines shown on property perimeter), crane operating plans must include Austin Energy facility clearance analysis. Implement the crane safety personnel pre-construction safety meeting requirement per UCM § 1.14.3.2 and specify minimum clearances: 20 feet for transmission facilities or 10 feet for distribution facilities per OSHA 1926.1400.

applicableAreas: Transformer pads and clearances to buildings, parking, and site features
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pad locations: (1) northwest corner near Building 1, (2) between Buildings 2 and 8, (3) between Buildings 4 and 5, and (4) between Buildings 6 and 7. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts these transformer pads in relation to buildings and parking areas. However, visual analysis of Sheet 21 found 'absolutely no dimensions, dashed clearance lines, or safety zones drawn or annotated around any of this equipment.' Similarly, analysis of Sheet 9 found 'no explicit clearance or setback dimensions shown between the Transformer Pad and the adjacent buildings, parking areas, or other site features.' UCM § 1.10.4 establishes specific minimum clearances for pad-mounted transformers and distribution vaults ranging from 5 feet to 20 feet depending on configuration and adjacent features.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 establishes mandatory minimum clearances from pad-mounted transformers: (1) Hot-stick use area (pad-locked sides) to adjacent building/structure: minimum 10 feet; (2) Hot-stick use area facing confined space (niche/vault): minimum 15 feet; (3) Oil-filled equipment to fire escape/stairs: minimum 20 feet horizontal/radial clearance; (4) Adjacent to brick/masonry building (2-hour fire rating): minimum 5 feet from side edges; (5) Adjacent to non-brick/masonry building: minimum 12 feet from oil-filled equipment; (6) Windows, doors, ventilating ducts: 5 feet lateral or 12 feet vertical if lateral less than 5 feet; (7) Equipment pads within 6 feet from parking/traffic areas must have truck access, and bollards required if within 4 feet; (8) Transformer pads must be 2 feet from back of sidewalks. The electrical site plan must show all four transformer locations with clearance dimensions to all adjacent buildings, parking areas, driveways, walkways, and fencing to demonstrate compliance. The absence of any clearance dimensions is the deficiency.
findings.comment: Add clearance dimensions to the electrical site plan for each of the four transformer pad locations per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4. For each pad, dimension the clearances to: adjacent buildings, parking areas, driveways, pedestrian walkways, fencing, mail kiosks, and any other site features. Specify clearances in feet (minimum 5-20 feet depending on configuration). Indicate bollard locations if pads are within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas. Specify sidewalk setback (minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalk) and truck access route (minimum 6 feet adjacent clearance). Add notes confirming compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 clearance requirements.
